title: Secretary of State of Massachusetts

context.text: The Green Papers lists incumbent Democrat William Galvin and Republican Anne Brensley as the two candidates in the November 3, 2026 general election for Secretary of the Commonwealth.

Galvin was the only name on the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary ballot (770,996 votes). Brensley was not on the Republican primary ballot and won the nomination as a write-in candidate (21,330 write-in votes for her, to 12,051 for all other write-ins).

candidates.name: William F. Galvin
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed.

record.text: Declined a July 2025 U.S. Department of Justice request for Massachusetts voters' full names, dates of birth, addresses, driver's license numbers and partial Social Security numbers, according to the ACLU of Massachusetts.

Was the named defendant in United States v. Galvin, in which the Justice Department sued for the voter data; a federal judge dismissed the suit on April 9, 2026, ruling the department had not stated the factual basis the statute requires. The ACLU's case page lists an appeal in the First Circuit.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or candidate statement of priorities could be loaded; the Secretary's office site (sec.state.ma.us) is behind a bot-protection block, so no direct quotes or issue positions are included. Record items come from news and the ACLU of Massachusetts case page, not from the Secretary's own releases; the July 2025 date is the month of the DOJ request as reported. Earlier-career biography from Ballotpedia was removed (Ballotpedia returns a WAF page).

candidates.name: Anne Brensley
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican nomination as a write-in candidate on September 1, 2026.

priorities.text: Encouraging business growth, engaging directly with disenfranchised voters, and protecting the integrity of the ballot.

Making Portuguese-language ballots available where needed, beginning with cities such as Fall River, and creating a Foreign Language Commission to review the accuracy of translated election materials.

candidates.researchNotes: No elected state record. No position on proof-of-citizenship requirements was found, so none is assigned.
